extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners interacting with USPTO office actions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners on citation practices, drafting complete and clear office actions, stating rejections, answering applicant arguments, and other prosecution-stage examiner responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC classification citation
rubrics_metrics.description: using the appropriate IPC subclass/group/subgroup. On the file wrapper 'Searched' box and PTO-892, the IPC subclass/group/subgroup shall be cited in the spaces provided for 'Classification.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the IPC subclass/group/subgroup is entered on the file wrapper 'Searched' box and on PTO-892 in the Classification field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific pages when relying on less than entire disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where less than the entire disclosure of the reference is relied upon, the sheet and page numbers specifically relied upon and the total number of sheets of drawing and pages of specification must be included (except applicant submitted citations). If the entire disclosure is relied on, the total number of sheets and pages are not required to be included on the PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sheet/page specifics and total counts when only part of a reference is relied upon; follow similar handling for foreign publications (e.g., German allowed applications). See MPEP § 901.05(a) for foreign-language date terms chart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient bibliographic information for publications
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing a publication, sufficient information should be given to determine the identity and facilitate the location of the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For books: provide data required by 37 CFR 1.104(d) (MPEP § 707.05) with specific pages relied on and STIC call number (do not cite the call number). For periodicals: give author(s), article title, periodical title, volume number, issue number, date, and pages. Minimal citations (author, title, date for books; periodical title, volume, date, pages for periodicals) may be used ONLY IF complete bibliographic details are unknown or unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpatent reference identification on PTO-892
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a nonpatent literature reference with a document identification number is cited, the identification number and the class and subclass should be included on form PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format provided: (S00840001) Winslow, C.E.A. Fresh Air and Ventilation ... TH 7653, W5, 315/22. If the original publication is located outside the Office, make or order a photocopy of at least the portion relied upon and indicate the class and subclass in which it will be filed, if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic document citation format (WIPO ST.14 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The format for the citation of an electronic document is as similar as possible to the format used for paper documents of the same type, but with the addition of certain information where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include (A) medium type in square brackets after title (e.g., [online], [CD-ROM]), (B) retrieval date in square brackets after publication date (four-digit year required), (C) 'Retrieved from' and the address/source, and (D) specific passages (pagination or first/last words) if possible. Retain Office copies of electronic documents if future retrieval may not be possible. If also available in paper form, electronic designation not required unless desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided citation examples for various electronic/media sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples are provided for documents retrieved from online databases, the Internet, CD-ROM, electronic serials, bulletin boards, email, datasheets, and patent office web databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the format illustrated by Examples 1-14 for proper citation of abstracts, online databases, Internet sources (include URL), CD-ROM products, electronic mail, bulletin boards, and web-hosted patent records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates for declassified printed matter
rubrics_metrics.description: There are usually two pertinent dates: the printing date and the publication date. The printing date may be considered as the date the material was prepared for limited distribution; the publication date is the date of release to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For anticipation purposes the date of release following declassification is the effective date of publication under the statute. Declassified printed matter may be prima facie evidence of prior knowledge as of its printing date for 35 U.S.C. 102(a), but that printing date may be antedated by affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131. If release date not shown, determine it from Office of Technical Services, Department of Commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting incorrect citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an error in citation of a reference is brought to the attention of the Office by applicant, a letter correcting the error, together with a correct copy of the reference, is sent to applicant. Where the error is discovered by the examiner, applicant is also notified and the period for reply restarted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should correct the error in ink on the paper, initial in the margin, and note the paper number of the action in which the citation has been correctly given. Use form paragraphs 7.81-7.83 for correction letters and supplying copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of court decisions and manuscript decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing court decisions, the USPQ citation should be given and, when convenient, the U.S., CCPA or Federal Reporter citation should also be provided. The citation of manuscript decisions which are not available to the public should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a manuscript decision is available to the public but not published, give the tribunal and complete data identifying the paper. Decisions found only in patent files should be cited only when there is no published decision on the same point. When citing Commissioner orders/notices/memoranda not yet in the manual, provide title and date and additional locating data when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call out formal requirements when subject matter is allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: As allowable subject matter has been indicated, applicant’s reply must either comply with all formal requirements or specifically traverse each requirement not complied with. See 37 CFR 1.111(b) and MPEP § 707.07(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is appropriate when changes must be made prior to allowance (e.g., drawing corrections or specification corrections). The action should call attention to 37 CFR 1.111(b) and state that a complete reply must comply or traverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of examiner's action
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s action will be complete as to all matters, except that in appropriate circumstances the action may be limited to such matters before further action is made. However, matters of form need not be raised by the examiner until a claim is found allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitations on completeness are appropriate in cases such as misjoinder, fundamental defects, or where informalities exist; otherwise address all relevant matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language to be used in rejecting claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claim is refused for any reason relating to the merits thereof it should be 'rejected' and the ground of rejection fully and clearly stated, and the word 'reject' must be used. The examiner should designate the statutory basis for any ground of rejection by express reference to a section of 35 U.S.C. in the opening sentence of each ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejected as broader than the enabling disclosure, give the reason; if indefinite point out where indefiniteness resides; if incomplete specify missing elements or advise what is required to render the claim complete. Avoid any personal language or expressions that the application is 'devoid of patentable subject matter' or that cast doubt on allowability of allowed claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify allowable claims and suggest amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should, as part of the first Office action on the merits, identify any claims which he or she judges, as presently recited, to be allowable and/or should suggest any way in which rejected claims may be amended to make them allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to do so implies to applicant that there appear to be no allowable claims. Where appropriate, suggest amendments to make claims allowable to expedite prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid improperly expressed rejections (omnibus/grouping)
rubrics_metrics.description: An omnibus rejection of the claim 'on the references and for the reasons of record' is stereotyped and usually not informative and should therefore be avoided. A plurality of claims should never be grouped together in a common rejection, unless that rejection is equally applicable to all claims in the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific grounds and explanations for each rejection and avoid blanket statements; separate grounds if different claims are rejected for different reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note all requirements outstanding in each letter
rubrics_metrics.description: In taking up an amended application for action the examiner should note in every letter all the requirements outstanding against the application. Every point in the prior action of an examiner which is still applicable must be repeated or referred to, to prevent the implied waiver of the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include requirements for information under 37 CFR 1.105 and determine whether any such requirement has been satisfied by negative reply under 1.105(a)(3). As soon as allowable subject matter is found, require correction of all informalities then present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer all material traversed and applicant arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the requirements are traversed, or suspension thereof requested, the examiner should make proper reference thereto in his or her action on the amendment. Where the applicant traverses any rejection, the examiner should, if he or she repeats the rejection, take note of the applicant’s argument and answer the substance of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rejection is applied to a new or amended claim, specifically identify that ground of rejection by citation of the paragraph in the former Office letter in which the rejection was originally stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address asserted advantages raised by applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant's reply includes arguments and affidavits that the prior art does not teach or inherently yield one or more advantages, and the examiner believes those advantages are not sufficient to overcome the rejection(s), the examiner should state the reasons for his or her position in the record, preferably in the action following the assertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By expressly addressing advantages, applicant and any reviewing Board will know the advantages were considered. See MPEP § 716 et seq. for treatment of affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use form paragraphs for unpersuasive or moot arguments (7.37–7.38)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.37 through 7.38 may be used where applicant's arguments are not persuasive or are moot because of new grounds of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs include specific scripted responses and must be preceded by paragraph 7.37 where indicated. Examples cover common argument types (age of references, bodily incorporation, hindsight reasoning, no suggestion to combine, nonanalogous art, number of references, results not contemplated by prior art, limitations not claimed, preamble weight, general allegation of patentability, intended use, etc.). When used, tailor bracketed insertions to the case and precede with required base paragraph(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to specific common unpersuasive arguments (categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific response principles provided for common applicant arguments: age of references, bodily incorporation, hindsight reasoning, no suggestion to combine, nonanalogous art, excessive number of references, obtaining result not contemplated by prior art, arguing limitations not claimed, preamble issues, general allegation of patentability, intended use, arguing references individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each form paragraph (e.g., 7.37.01 through 7.37.13) must be preceded by 7.37 and contains examiner notes on how to fill bracketed items. Apply the cited case law (e.g., In re Keller, In re McLaughlin, In re Fine, In re Oetiker, etc.) where relevant and explain why the argument is unpersuasive per the provided templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid piecemeal examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Piecemeal examination should be avoided as much as possible. The examiner ordinarily should reject each claim on all valid grounds available, avoiding undue multiplication of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major technical rejections (lack of proper disclosure, lack of enablement, serious indefiniteness, res judicata) should be applied where appropriate even if there may be a sufficient prior-art rejection. When a major technical rejection is proper, fully develop reasons rather than a mere conclusion. Do not usually add secondary minor technical rejections when a sound prior-art rejection discloses the 'heart' of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations permitting limited action on claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Some situations exist where examination appears best accomplished by limiting action on the claims to a particular issue, such as when an application is too informal for complete action, undue multiplicity of claims with no election, misjoinder of inventions with no election, or disclosure directed to perpetual motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases address the specific issue (e.g., request election, address informality) and cite appropriate MPEP sections (e.g., §702.01, §2173.05(n), §803, §806.02, §812.01). For perpetual motion cases, still cite best prior art available but do not necessarily apply it to the claims; conversely, certain rejections (res judicata, new matter, no prima facie showing for reissue, inoperativeness) should be accompanied by rejection on all other available grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify of inaccuracies in amendment (see §714.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriate, notify of inaccuracies in amendments as directed in MPEP § 714.23.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the cited MPEP section for procedures and wording when notifying applicants of inaccuracies in amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention each pending claim and provide claim status summary
rubrics_metrics.description: In every office action, each pending claim should be mentioned by number, and its treatment or status given. Each action should conclude with a summary of all claims presented for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims retained under 37 CFR 1.142 and 1.146 should be treated per MPEP § 821–821.03 and § 809.02(c). Keep the Index of Claims up to date (MPEP § 719.04) and follow special treatment for claims in interference or losing party applications (see §2363.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft claims for pro se inventor-filed applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When, during examination of a pro se application it becomes apparent that there is patentable subject matter disclosed, the examiner should draft one or more claims for the applicant and indicate in the action that such claims would be allowed if incorporated in the application by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice is desirable to expedite prosecution and is expected to be applied in all cases where it is apparent the applicant is unfamiliar with proper preparation and prosecution of patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require correction of informalities once allowable subject matter is found
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as allowable subject matter is found, correction of all informalities then present should be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie this requirement to the formalities notice per 37 CFR 1.111(b) and ensure applicant complies or traverses each formal requirement not met.
